hero.headline: Senate Republicans and Trump at odds over surveillance, Iran policy, and filibuster
hero.teaser: Senate Majority Leader John Barrasso faces disagreements with the White House on multiple fronts as Congress returns from recess.
hero.body:
Senate Republicans Reject War Powers Resolution After Trump Pressure

President Trump faced off with Senate Republicans over military action in Iran, culminating in a dramatic reversal that underscores deepening tensions between the White House and GOP lawmakers.

The conflict began when Senate Republicans allowed a vote on a war powers resolution to block Trump's Iran operations. Angered by this defiance, Trump summoned GOP senators to a contentious lunch on Capitol Hill where he berated them over their opposition to his military strategy.

The confrontation grew particularly heated between Trump and Louisiana Senator Bill Cassidy, one of four Republicans who voted with Democrats on the measure. Trump questioned why anyone would support the War Powers Act. Cassidy responded directly, asking whether the question was rhetorical or genuine.

Despite the tense exchange, Cassidy's position shifted dramatically hours later. After receiving a personal briefing at the White House from Vice President JD Vance and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Cassidy returned to Capitol Hill and voted against a nearly identical war powers resolution that came up for a separate vote that evening.

"I want to thank Vice President Vance and Special Envoy Witkoff for the thorough briefing this afternoon on Iran," Cassidy posted on social media afterward. "I appreciate the quick invitation to the White House to address many of my concerns."

Republican Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky also shifted his stance, voting present on the second measure "to give the President more space and leverage to negotiate a lasting peace," according to his social media statement. Paul had previously voted with Democrats on the initial resolution.

The second war powers measure failed 47-50-1 just before midnight Wednesday, after which the Senate departed for a two-week recess. Senate Majority Leader John Thune and other GOP colleagues called Trump following the vote. Thune reported to reporters that Trump was "pleased with the outcome."

Trump subsequently thanked Thune in a social media post, noting that Cassidy and Paul had changed their positions. "This vote puts Iran on notice!" Trump wrote.

The two war powers votes occurred on separate tracks but addressed nearly identical concerns. Both measures were largely symbolic and do not carry the full force of law. The first passed the House and was then blocked by the Senate on Tuesday, followed by the second failed Senate vote on Wednesday.

The disputes over Iran policy form part of a broader disagreement between Trump and Senate Republicans. The two sides also remain at odds over extending surveillance authorities and Trump's push to eliminate the Senate filibuster to advance his legislative agenda, a proposal many Republican senators oppose as it would undermine their ability to block future Democratic initiatives.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes 15 Russian Ships on Key Trade Route
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces bombed Russian vessels in the Sea of Azov, forcing Moscow to suspend shipping in the strategic waterway.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drone strikes targeted 15 Russian ships in the Sea of Azov near Crimea, forcing Russia to suspend shipping operations on a critical trade route connecting Russian ports to international waters through the Black Sea.

The attacks are part of Ukraine's broader campaign to damage Russian military and economic capabilities. Ukrainian forces have systematically struck Russian oil tankers and refineries to disrupt fuel supplies and logistics. One person was killed in the latest strikes on Russian territory.

cards.headline: Ground Robots Transform Warfare on Ukrainian Battlefields
cards.teaser: Ukraine has deployed ground robots that began as supply vehicles but now evacuate wounded soldiers, hold defensive positions, and engage in combat.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces are using ground robots for an expanding range of battlefield roles, from medical evacuation to holding trenches and conducting lethal operations. The machines started as supply mules but have evolved into versatile combat tools that are reshaping ground warfare.

Ukraine has become a leader in military drone innovation during its war with Russia. The introduction of armed ground robots represents another technological adaptation by Ukrainian forces seeking advantages against a larger adversary. The robots can operate in dangerous areas where human soldiers face high casualty risks.

cards.headline: TSMC Reports 36 Percent Sales Jump Driven by AI Demand
cards.teaser: The world's largest contract chipmaker posted record second-quarter revenue as artificial intelligence spending continued to accelerate.
cards.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company posted record second-quarter revenue, driven by surging demand for advanced artificial intelligence chips. June alone saw a 68 percent year-over-year revenue increase.

The company is struggling to keep pace with orders. Its CoWoS advanced packaging technology, crucial for high-performance AI chips, faces supply constraints as demand outpaces production capacity. Some customers are turning to competitors including Intel and other Taiwanese manufacturers to fulfill their orders.

cards.headline: Europe Considers Social Media Ban for Children
cards.teaser: The European Commission is weighing rule changes across its 27 member nations following the release of a new report on child safety online.
cards.body:
The European Union is weighing sweeping new restrictions on how children and teenagers access social media. Potential measures include age limits, outright bans, and phased access to platforms. The European Commission is considering these rule changes across all 27 EU member states.

Under the proposed regulations, social media platforms could be required to prove their services are safe for young users before allowing access. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has supported the initiative. The restrictions would significantly reshape how major tech companies operate across the continent.

cards.headline: Wall Street Banks Set to Report Second Quarter Earnings
cards.teaser: Major financial institutions will release quarterly results this week after collecting substantial fees from the SpaceX IPO and large merger deals.
cards.body:
Five major U.S. banks will begin reporting second-quarter results next week. The earnings releases come after a busy period for investment banking, with Wall Street firms collecting substantial fees from the SpaceX initial public offering and several significant mergers and acquisitions completed during the quarter.

The quarterly reports will show how banks performed across their consumer, commercial, and investment banking divisions. These results will serve as an important indicator of the financial sector's health and overall market conditions during a period marked by heightened deal-making activity.

cards.headline: Congress returns with limited time and lengthy agenda
cards.teaser: Lawmakers face the loss of a senator, multiple policy debates, and a compressed legislative calendar.
cards.body:
Congress reconvenes this week with a lengthy to-do list and limited time before the fall elections. Lawmakers return to the sudden loss of a senator and pressure to address pending legislation on surveillance, defense policy, and appropriations.

The compressed calendar leaves little room for extended debates or procedural delays. House and Senate leaders will need to prioritize which measures to advance before the August recess and the final push before voters head to the polls in November.

cards.headline: Fire at Bangkok Bar Kills 27, Injures 73
cards.teaser: A fire engulfed a music venue in Bangkok's Chatuchak district, killing at least 27 people as patrons fled through flames.
cards.body:
A massive fire swept through a pub in Bangkok's Chatuchak district, killing at least 27 people and injuring 73 others. Firefighters arriving at the scene found patrons desperately running through flames to escape the burning building. Footage from first responders shows a huge blaze with plumes of smoke pouring from the pub's front entrance.

At least 25 of the injured are in critical condition. The fire erupted at the popular music venue in the northern part of Thailand's capital. Authorities are investigating the circumstances that led to the blaze.

cards.headline: Wildfire South of Paris May Have Been Set Deliberately
cards.teaser: A French minister said a wildfire burning south of Paris could have been deliberately started, marking an unusual fire threat to the capital region.
cards.body:
French authorities deployed firefighting planes from southern France to combat a massive wildfire in the Fontainebleau forest southeast of Paris. A minister indicated the fire may have been deliberately set. The deployment marked the first time aircraft typically used in the drier south were sent to tackle fires near the capital.

The blaze began late Sunday afternoon in the former royal hunting preserve, about 40 miles from Paris. It swept across approximately 800 hectares of forest and continued spreading Monday. Officials described it as exceptional in scale, with 900 homes evacuated and significant disruptions to road and rail links in the region.

cards.headline: Israel Attempted to Recruit Former Iranian President as Asset
cards.teaser: Israeli intelligence conducted a yearslong effort to cultivate Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as an asset, culminating in a failed plan to bring him to a safe house.
cards.body:
Israel spent years grooming former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as an intelligence asset, according to reports on the covert operation. The effort reached its peak when Israeli operatives attempted to take Ahmadinejad to a safe house in the early days of the current conflict between Israel and Iran.

The plan ultimately fell apart before Israeli intelligence could complete the operation. Ahmadinejad served as Iran's president from 2005 to 2013 and was known for his confrontational stance toward Israel and the West during his tenure.

cards.headline: Lebanese Residents Remain in War-Torn Towns Despite Israeli Occupation Threat
cards.teaser: Residents of southern Lebanon are staying in their homes despite widespread destruction from fighting between Israel and Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Entire towns in southern Lebanon have been emptied by fighting between Israel and Hezbollah, yet some residents have chosen to stay. Those who remain fear that evacuating would mean permanent loss of their homes and communities.

The conflict has caused widespread destruction across southern Lebanon. Residents who have not fled face ongoing danger from the fighting but view leaving as too great a risk to their property and way of life.

cards.headline: Ground Robots Transform Warfare on Ukrainian Battlefields
cards.teaser: Ukraine has deployed ground robots that began as supply vehicles but now evacuate wounded soldiers, hold defensive positions, and engage in combat.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces are using ground robots for an expanding range of battlefield roles, from medical evacuation to holding trenches and conducting lethal operations. The machines started as supply mules but have evolved into versatile combat tools that are reshaping ground warfare.

The introduction of armed ground robots represents another technological adaptation by Ukrainian forces seeking advantages against a larger adversary. The robots can operate in dangerous areas where human soldiers face high casualty risks.

cards.headline: Ukraine Shifts Focus to Psychological Operations Against Russia
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces are expanding their use of psychological warfare techniques aimed at undermining Russian public support for the war.
cards.body:
Ukraine is turning its attention to psychological operations designed to weaken Russian support for the ongoing conflict. Ukrainian officials, who have already demonstrated innovation in drone technology, are now focusing on information campaigns targeting Russian audiences.

The shift represents a new phase in Ukraine's war strategy as the conflict continues. Psychological operations aim to influence enemy morale and public opinion, complementing conventional military efforts. Ukraine has sought various methods to counter Russia's numerical advantages throughout the war.

hero.headline: Federal prison guards retaliate against inmates who file complaints, investigation finds
hero.body:
Federal prisoners who file complaints about mistreatment often face retaliation from guards, according to an investigation by NPR and The Marshall Project. The investigation examined how the prison complaint system, designed to allow inmates to report abuse and misconduct, frequently becomes a mechanism for further harm rather than accountability.

Prisoners are legally permitted to submit grievances about their treatment in federal facilities. The system is intended to provide a formal avenue for addressing problems ranging from medical neglect to physical abuse. However, the investigation found that exercising this right commonly results in punishment or harassment from correctional staff.

The practice creates a significant barrier to oversight within the federal prison system. When inmates fear retaliation for reporting problems, violations of prison rules and law can continue unchecked. The investigation documented patterns of guards responding to complaints by escalating restrictions, moving prisoners to less favorable housing, or creating other difficulties for those who speak up.

The federal Bureau of Prisons operates more than 120 facilities housing approximately 160,000 inmates. The complaint system serves as one of the few ways prisoners can seek remedies for poor conditions or abusive treatment without access to outside legal help. When that system functions as a tool for retaliation rather than accountability, it undermines the basic protections meant to prevent abuse in custody.

The investigation arrives as federal prisons face ongoing scrutiny over staffing shortages, aging infrastructure, and questions about how facilities handle everything from medical care to violence prevention. The findings suggest that structural problems extend beyond resource constraints to include a culture where reporting problems carries personal risk for those in custody.

cards.headline: Memphis task force agent shoots man during mental health crisis
cards.teaser: A Homeland Security Investigations agent shot a 25-year-old man during a mental health crisis in Memphis.
cards.body:
Jonah Neal, 25, was shot by a Homeland Security Investigations agent in May while experiencing a mental health crisis. The shooting occurred when members of a multi-agency task force responded to the situation.

The incident is at least the fourth deadly shooting connected to the task force, raising concerns about how law enforcement handles mental health emergencies and the involvement of federal task forces in local policing.

cards.headline: Mitch McConnell leaves hospital after fall and pneumonia
cards.teaser: Senator Mitch McConnell disclosed he was hospitalized following a fall that led to pneumonia, breaking weeks of silence.
cards.body:
Senator Mitch McConnell has left the hospital following treatment for a fall and pneumonia. The 84-year-old Kentucky Republican broke weeks of silence with a statement revealing the fall had led to his hospitalization. Doctors conducted a battery of tests to determine the cause of his fall.

McConnell said he will not return to work immediately. In his statement, he acknowledged that people of his generation often hesitate to discuss the vulnerability that comes with aging, explaining his earlier silence about his condition.

cards.headline: Colorado passes law to address electric vehicle battery recycling costs
cards.teaser: A new Colorado law aims to solve the problem of electric vehicle batteries that cost more to recycle than their salvage value.
cards.body:
Colorado enacted legislation to address a fundamental challenge in EV battery recycling: for some batteries, the cost to recycle them exceeds the value of the materials recovered. This economic imbalance creates both financial and environmental problems as more electric vehicles reach the end of their lifespan.

The new law establishes a framework designed to make battery recycling financially viable. As electric vehicle adoption accelerates, the industry and environmental regulators are grappling with solutions to ensure spent batteries are managed sustainably rather than becoming waste.

cards.headline: Heatwave returns to UK as wildfires continue burning
cards.teaser: Heat and humidity are building again across the UK after a brief temperature drop, as wildfires burn in multiple areas.
cards.body:
The UK is experiencing a prolonged heatwave, with temperatures exceeding 34C for the eighth day this year—breaking the previous annual record of seven consecutive days. Many areas are now under hosepipe bans as millions grapple with the intense conditions.

After a brief respite, temperatures and humidity are set to rise again this week as the heatwave intensifies. Wildfires continue burning across the country, compounding challenges for emergency services and residents in affected areas.

cards.headline: Wildfire near Paris may have been deliberately set, French minister says
cards.teaser: A minister said a wildfire burning south of Paris could have been started intentionally, marking an unusual fire event for the region.
cards.body:
French authorities are investigating whether a major wildfire in the Fontainebleau forest, about 40 miles southeast of Paris, was deliberately set. The blaze began late Sunday and rapidly spread across roughly 800 hectares of forest, prompting the evacuation of 900 homes and disrupting road and rail links in the region.

The fire's scale and proximity to the capital prompted an unusual response: firefighting aircraft were deployed from southern France for the first time to assist with blazes near Paris. These planes are normally stationed in France's drier southern regions where wildfires are more common, highlighting how exceptional this fire threat to the Paris area has become.

cards.headline: Witness describes escape from Bangkok bar fire
cards.teaser: A musician performing when a fire broke out at a Bangkok bar said he crawled toward an exit and was thrown from the building by an explosion.
cards.body:
A musician performing at a Bangkok bar crawled toward the exit as fire swept through the venue. He was thrown from the building when something exploded during the blaze.

Firefighters responding to the scene in the Chatuchak district found patrons running through flames to escape. The fire killed at least 27 people and left 25 critically injured.

hero.headline: TSMC Reports 36 Percent Sales Jump Driven by AI Demand
hero.teaser: The world's largest contract chipmaker posted record second-quarter revenue as artificial intelligence spending continued to accelerate.
hero.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company posted record second-quarter revenue, driven by surging demand for advanced artificial intelligence chips. June alone saw a 68 percent year-over-year revenue increase.

The company is struggling to keep pace with orders. Its CoWoS advanced packaging technology, crucial for high-performance AI chips, faces supply constraints as demand outpaces production capacity. Some customers are turning to competitors including Intel and other Taiwanese manufacturers to fulfill their orders.

cards.headline: SK Hynix Shares Fall in Seoul After US Listing Debut
cards.teaser: The South Korean chipmaker's stock dropped in its home market following a highly anticipated Nasdaq debut that became the largest US listing by a foreign company.
cards.body:
SK Hynix completed a record-breaking US listing on Friday, raising $26.5 billion through a Nasdaq debut that ranks among the world's largest stock offerings by a foreign company. The shares initially surged as much as 17% during US trading, reflecting strong investor demand.

However, the momentum reversed in Seoul's premarket trading, where SK Hynix shares declined 10 percent. The divergence between the enthusiastic US market response and the Seoul selling pressure suggests investors are reassessing valuations following the listing. The chip supplier has capitalized on surging demand for advanced memory chips driven by the global race to build AI datacentres.

cards.headline: SpaceX Valuation Debate Continues One Month After IPO
cards.teaser: Analysts remain divided on the space company's worth as investors gain clearer understanding of its revenue sources.
cards.body:
A month after SpaceX's historic initial public offering, investors have gained insight into how the company currently generates revenue. The clearer picture of SpaceX's business operations—spanning launch services, Starlink satellite internet, and other ventures—has helped bring the company's valuation into sharper focus.

Wall Street analysts remain divided on SpaceX's prospects, with some projecting shares could reach $220 by the end of 2026. The IPO generated substantial fees for investment banks involved in the offering, while analysts continue to assess the company's business fundamentals amid varying price targets.

cards.headline: Europe Considers Social Media Ban for Children
cards.teaser: The European Commission is weighing rule changes across its 27 member nations following the release of a new report on child safety online.
cards.body:
The European Union is weighing sweeping new restrictions on how children and teenagers access social media. Potential measures include age limits, outright bans, and phased access to platforms. The European Commission is considering these rule changes across all 27 EU member states.

Under the proposed regulations, social media platforms could be required to prove their services are safe for young users before allowing access. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has supported the initiative. The restrictions would significantly reshape how major tech companies operate across the continent.

cards.headline: Wall Street Banks Set to Report Second Quarter Earnings
cards.teaser: Major financial institutions will release quarterly results this week after collecting substantial fees from the SpaceX IPO and large merger deals.
cards.body:
Five major U.S. banks will begin reporting second-quarter results next week. The earnings releases come after a busy period for investment banking, with Wall Street firms collecting substantial fees from the SpaceX initial public offering and several significant mergers and acquisitions completed during the quarter.

The quarterly reports will show how banks performed across their consumer, commercial, and investment banking divisions. These results will serve as an important indicator of the financial sector's health and overall market conditions during a period marked by heightened deal-making activity.

cards.headline: Colorado Addresses Economics of Electric Vehicle Battery Recycling
cards.teaser: The state has developed a solution to the economic challenges facing the EV battery recycling industry.
cards.body:
As more electric vehicles reach the end of their lifespan, used batteries will accumulate in growing numbers. Recycling these batteries recovers valuable materials like lithium, cobalt, and nickel, but the process faces a fundamental challenge: it often costs more to recycle a battery than the recovered materials are worth.

Colorado has enacted a new law designed to solve this economics problem. The state's approach aims to make battery recycling financially viable while addressing the environmental concerns of improper disposal, potentially serving as a model for other regions grappling with the same issue.

cards.headline: Private Aviation Booms for World Cup Travel
cards.teaser: Wealthy attendees are using helicopters and private aircraft to reach matches, creating heavy air traffic above the Hamptons.
cards.body:
The skies above the Hamptons have become crowded with helicopters as wealthy individuals travel to World Cup games. The concentration of private aviation highlights the stark inequality in how different groups access major sporting events. Charter helicopter services have seen a surge in bookings for match days.

The phenomenon reflects broader patterns in luxury travel and sports tourism. Private aircraft allow passengers to avoid commercial airline schedules and ground traffic congestion around stadiums. The trend has created a visible disparity between fans arriving by private helicopter and those using public transportation or personal vehicles.

hero.headline: Rare meteorite reveals evidence of lost Moon-sized world from early solar system
hero.body:
A rare meteorite examined in 2026 has revealed evidence of a Moon-sized world that orbited the young Sun more than 4.5 billion years ago before vanishing from the solar system. The ancient body existed during the period when Earth was still forming, then disappeared in what scientists believe may have been a catastrophic collision.

The meteorite analysis provides a glimpse into the chaotic early solar system, when planetary bodies were still coalescing and collisions were common. The Moon-sized world would have been comparable to Mars in scale, orbiting among the other developing planets during a period of intense bombardment and gravitational interactions.

Scientists working with the meteorite found chemical signatures that could only have come from a planetary body of substantial size. The evidence suggests this world existed for a period before being destroyed, likely shattered in an impact with another large object during the violent early phase of solar system formation.

The discovery adds to understanding of how the solar system evolved from a disk of gas and dust into the arrangement of planets seen today. During the first several hundred million years after the Sun formed, dozens of planetary bodies competed for space and material. Many of these early worlds collided with each other or were ejected from the solar system entirely through gravitational interactions.

According to researchers at Curtin University, the early solar system was vastly different from what we see now. Earth itself was mostly a water world with few pieces of continental crust, while the Sun would have been dimmer and the Moon closer to our planet. Early life existed in the form of stromatolites, a type of cyanobacteria similar to algae.

During this period known as the Archean eon, meteorite impacts were continuous. Evidence of these collisions remains visible on the Moon's surface, but on Earth they have largely been erased through erosion, subduction and plate tectonics. Finding preserved evidence of these ancient impact events is therefore exceptionally significant for scientists.

The meteorite that preserved evidence of this lost world survived the intervening 4.5 billion years before falling to Earth and being recovered for study. Meteorites serve as time capsules from the early solar system, containing materials and chemical records that predate Earth's oldest rocks.

Associate professor Bruce Schaefer from Macquarie University described the research as "a real detective story," noting that the combination of techniques used to analyse the meteorite was clever and innovative. He emphasized that discovering physical evidence of these ancient events is particularly exciting because while scientists know such impacts must have occurred, actually observing them provides powerful confirmation.

This particular specimen has proven especially valuable for reconstructing the population of bodies that existed in the young solar system but left no other trace of their existence.

cards.headline: Chinese spacecraft approaches unidentified object near Earth
cards.teaser: A Chinese spacecraft is moving toward a mysterious object in near-Earth space.
cards.body:
A Chinese spacecraft has begun approaching an unidentified object located in the vicinity of Earth. The mission represents an effort to investigate the nature of the object, which has drawn attention from space monitoring programs.

The spacecraft's approach is being tracked as it closes distance with the target. Chinese space authorities are conducting the operation as part of ongoing space surveillance activities.

cards.headline: Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold images leak showing new Pine color and redesigned camera
cards.teaser: Leaked images of Google's upcoming Pixel 11 Pro Fold show a new color option and camera changes.
cards.body:
Images of the unreleased Pixel 11 Pro Fold have surfaced online, revealing Google's Pine color option and a modified camera design. The leaked photos show a sleeker camera module compared to previous Pixel Fold models.

Google has scheduled a launch event for August 12, where the Pixel 11 lineup is expected to be unveiled. The leaked materials also suggest possible price increases for the new device generation compared to current models.

cards.headline: Perseid meteor shower returns this week with up to 100 meteors per hour visible
cards.teaser: The annual Perseid meteor shower begins this week, offering viewers across the United States a chance to see dozens of meteors hourly.
cards.body:
The Perseid meteor shower, one of the most active meteor events of the year, is beginning this week with viewing opportunities across the United States. The shower is expected to produce up to 100 meteors per hour at its peak, making it one of the most productive annual meteor events.

This year's Perseids will appear under an Earthshine moon, affecting visibility conditions for observers. The meteor shower occurs annually when Earth passes through debris left by the Swift-Tuttle comet.

cards.headline: South Dakota Tyrannosaurus rex fossil could sell for $30 million at auction
cards.teaser: A Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton from South Dakota is expected to fetch $30 million or more at auction, potentially becoming the most expensive fossil ever sold.
cards.body:
A Tyrannosaurus rex fossil known as "Gus" is scheduled to go to auction on Tuesday with an estimated value of $30 million, potentially making it the most expensive dinosaur fossil ever sold. The specimen was discovered in South Dakota.

The sale has sparked concern among scientists who worry that private auctions remove important specimens from research institutions and museums. High prices at dinosaur fossil auctions make it increasingly difficult for educational institutions to acquire these specimens for study and public display.

cards.headline: Pokémon Go marks 10 years with millions still playing mobile game
cards.teaser: The mobile game Pokémon Go has reached its 10th anniversary with millions of active players continuing to participate.
cards.body:
Pokémon Go celebrated its 10th anniversary with a major in-person event in Times Square, where nearly 2,000 players gathered simultaneously to battle Mewtwo together. Organisers described it as one of the largest Pokémon battles held in history.

Michael Steranka, vice president at Scopely, the game's owner, emphasised that bringing people together has always been central to the game's mission. The company launched a Summer Quest event as part of the anniversary celebrations, with plans for additional 10th anniversary activities ahead.

cards.headline: Assassin's Creed Black Flag remake became unplayable during Ubisoft Connect outage
cards.teaser: Players of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced were unable to access the game during a Ubisoft Connect service disruption, despite the game including an offline mode.
cards.body:
The recently released Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced remake became completely unplayable when Ubisoft Connect experienced a service outage. The issue prevented players from accessing the game even though it includes an offline mode feature.

The incident highlighted ongoing concerns about always-online requirements for games that theoretically support offline play. Ubisoft Connect serves as the authentication and distribution platform for Ubisoft games across multiple platforms.

hero.headline: Ryan Blaney wins NASCAR Cup race at Atlanta in overtime thriller
hero.body:
Ryan Blaney captured the NASCAR Cup Series race at Atlanta Motor Speedway after a dramatic overtime finish. The race concluded following a three-hour weather delay that pushed the competition deep into the evening. Blaney navigated the final laps as chaos unfolded behind him, securing the victory in what became one of the most unpredictable finishes of the season.

Bubba Wallace was penalized on the final lap, adding to the drama of the overtime restart. The penalty altered the final running order and became a focal point of post-race discussion. NASCAR officials conducted post-race inspections on all competing vehicles, standard procedure following Cup Series events at Atlanta.

The race at EchoPark saw multiple lead changes throughout the day before weather forced officials to halt competition. When racing resumed, drivers faced challenging track conditions and aggressive strategies as teams gambled on fuel and tire management. The extended delay meant crews had to recalibrate their approaches for the final run to the checkered flag.

Atlanta Motor Speedway has produced some of the closest finishes in NASCAR history, and this race added to that legacy. The track's reconfiguration in recent years has led to pack racing and photo finishes that keep fans engaged until the final moments. Blaney's victory marked his latest success at a venue known for rewarding both skill and good fortune.

The win strengthens Blaney's position in the Cup Series standings as the season approaches its midpoint. With playoff implications looming, every victory carries additional weight for drivers hoping to secure their postseason spots. The Atlanta race demonstrated once again why weather delays and late-race restarts remain among the most unpredictable elements in stock car racing.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark breaks WNBA record as Fever defeat defending champion Aces
cards.teaser: The Indiana Fever beat the Las Vegas Aces for the second time this season, with Caitlin Clark adding to her rookie accomplishments.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark scored 12 points in 24 minutes as the Indiana Fever defeated the Las Vegas Aces in Las Vegas. The win marked the second time this season Indiana has beaten the defending WNBA champions. Clark broke a WNBA record during the game, though specific details of the record were not provided in reports.

The Fever dominated the Aces throughout the contest, closing out their road trip with a convincing performance. Las Vegas struggled to contain Indiana's offense despite the home court advantage. The victory continues Indiana's strong season and raises questions about the Aces' ability to defend their championship.

cards.headline: Paddy Pimblett submits Benoit Saint-Denis at UFC 329
cards.teaser: British fighter Paddy Pimblett produced a dominant performance at UFC 329, finishing his opponent by submission.
cards.body:
Paddy Pimblett defeated Benoit Saint-Denis via submission at UFC 329, delivering what observers called a superstar moment for the Liverpool fighter. After the victory, Pimblett stated he could replicate the performance against former lightweight champion Charles Oliveira. The win continues Pimblett's rise through the UFC ranks.

The UFC 329 card was headlined by Conor McGregor versus Max Holloway in their rematch. Prize money bonuses were distributed to several fighters on the card, including Pimblett for his submission victory. Mixed martial arts professionals reacted to the performance on social media, with some suggesting a potential matchup between Pimblett and featherweight champion Ilia Topuria.

cards.headline: England advance to World Cup semi-finals, will face Argentina
cards.teaser: England reached the World Cup semi-finals and are set for a high-profile clash with Argentina and Lionel Messi.
cards.body:
England advanced to the World Cup semi-finals after defeating Norway in Miami. Thomas Tuchel's team will face Argentina, the reigning champions, on Wednesday in Atlanta. This marks the first competitive meeting between the nations since the 2002 World Cup.

The semi-final is shaping up as one of football's biggest grudge matches, with significant historical rivalry between the teams. England will compete for a place in the final against either France or Spain.

cards.headline: Ted Lasso actor Cristo Fernandez makes professional football debut
cards.teaser: Cristo Fernandez, known for his role in the television series Ted Lasso, played his first professional match for El Paso Locomotive.
cards.body:
Cristo Fernandez, known for his role in the Apple TV series Ted Lasso, has made his professional football debut with El Paso Locomotive, a second-tier American soccer club competing in the USL Championship.

The actor's transition to professional sports has garnered attention given his television profile. Fernandez's move represents a return to football rather than a new venture, as he played the sport before pursuing his acting career.

cards.headline: AJ Dybantsa leads Washington Wizards to Summer League victory
cards.teaser: Top prospect AJ Dybantsa delivered another strong performance in NBA Summer League play, leading the Wizards past the Kings.
cards.body:
AJ Dybantsa impressed in NBA Summer League action as the Washington Wizards defeated the Sacramento Kings. Dybantsa led the Wizards in scoring during what may have been his final summer league appearance. The highly touted prospect has drawn significant attention from scouts and analysts throughout the summer circuit.

Darius Acuff Jr. also contributed to Washington's victory over Sacramento. The Wizards built on positives from their first game of the summer league, showing improved cohesion and execution. Summer league games allow teams to evaluate young talent and provide developmental opportunities for players hoping to earn regular season roster spots.

cards.headline: FIFA official cleared USMNT's Folarin Balogun to face Belgium without full review
cards.teaser: A single FIFA official waived a suspension that would have kept U.S. forward Folarin Balogun out of a World Cup match against Belgium.
cards.body:
Only one FIFA official was involved in the decision to clear United States men's national team player Folarin Balogun to play against Belgium. The decision waived a ban that would have sidelined Balogun for the World Cup match. President Trump reportedly asked FIFA to review the suspension before the official's intervention.

Balogun was eligible to play after the ruling, participating in a match that saw Belgium heavily defeated by the United States. Broadcaster JP Dellacamera called his final World Cup game during the tournament. The decision to allow Balogun to play has raised questions about FIFA's procedures for handling player eligibility and suspension reviews during major tournaments.

hero.headline: Sam Neill, Jurassic Park and Peaky Blinders Actor, Dies at 78
hero.body:
Sam Neill, the New Zealand actor celebrated for roles in Jurassic Park, The Piano, and Peaky Blinders, died on Monday at age 78. His family announced the death through a statement posted on his Instagram account, describing it as "sudden and unexpected." Neill passed away in Sydney, Australia, surrounded by family members.

Neill had recently announced that he was cancer-free following a diagnosis of stage three angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, a rare blood cancer, in 2022. Though he had recovered from the disease, he continued receiving monthly chemotherapy treatments. In his 2023 memoir, Neill discussed his year of chemotherapy and expressed his philosophy about mortality, saying he was not afraid to die but would prefer to live another decade or two to see his farm and grandchildren flourish.

Born Nigel John Dermot Neill in 1947 in Omagh, Northern Ireland, he adopted the name Sam at age 12, finding it easier to navigate the world with that identity. His family relocated to New Zealand in 1954. After initially studying law at university in Christchurch, Neill turned to acting, joining the Downstage Theatre in Wellington as a professional actor earning modest wages supplemented by leftover kitchen food.

His breakthrough came with the 1977 film Sleeping Dogs, the first New Zealand film to gain distribution in the United States. This led to roles in major productions including My Brilliant Career, Omen III, and The Hunt for Red October. In 1993, Neill achieved widespread international recognition through two simultaneous performances: as the romantic lead in Jane Campion's Oscar-winning The Piano and as Dr. Alan Grant in Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park. Though the role was originally offered to Harrison Ford, Neill's portrayal defined his career for global audiences. He reprised the character in Jurassic Park III and Jurassic World Dominion.

Throughout his five-decade career, Neill accumulated more than 150 credits across film and television. He became known for playing charismatic romantic leads and complex villains in productions ranging from blockbuster films to independent cinema. His television work included the role of corrupt Major Chester Campbell in the British crime drama Peaky Blinders. He was even considered as a successor to Roger Moore for the James Bond franchise, completing a screen test in 1986, though Timothy Dalton ultimately secured the role.

Beyond his acting career, Neill owned Two Paddocks, a farm and winery in Central Otago, New Zealand's wine region. He humorously named farm animals after fellow actors, including a chicken named Laura Dern, a duck named Kylie Minogue, and a cow named Helena Bonham Carter.

Directors, actors, and collaborators paid tribute following his death, with Jurassic World Dominion director Colin Trevorrow describing Neill as "a deeply soulful and beautiful man" whose strength supported those around him.

cards.headline: Madonna's Confessions II Debuts at No. 1 on Album Chart
cards.teaser: The pop star secures her tenth number one album with Confessions II, extending her record as a chart performer.
cards.body:
Madonna's latest album, Confessions II, debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 chart, marking her tenth chart-topping album. The release extends her decades-long dominance in popular music, with her first number one album coming more than 40 years ago.

The album's success places Madonna and Michael Jackson together in the Billboard 200's top 10 for the first time in 25 years. Ken Carson and Sienna Spiro also debuted in the top 10 alongside Madonna's release.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Closes Yankee Stadium Residency With Late-Night Performance
cards.teaser: The rapper concluded his three-show Yankee Stadium run with a marathon set featuring appearances by Beyoncé, Rihanna, and Usher.
cards.body:
Jay-Z concluded his three-night Yankee Stadium residency on Sunday with an extended show that he promised would continue until 5 a.m. The performance celebrated 30 years since his landmark debut album Reasonable Doubt, showcasing the rapper performing the album's tracks in sequence with visually stunning production.

The closing concert featured special guest appearances and marked a homecoming celebration for the Brooklyn native. The residency highlighted Jay-Z's enduring legacy as one of hip-hop's greatest MCs, demonstrating why his career has remained brilliant across three decades of music and cultural influence.

cards.headline: Sacha Baron Cohen Brings Back Ali G at Wimbledon Men's Final
cards.teaser: The comedian revived his character Ali G at the Wimbledon championship match, appearing in character ahead of a new film.
cards.body:
Sacha Baron Cohen revived his comedy character Ali G at the Wimbledon men's final on Sunday, appearing among the surprise special guests at the championship match. The character made an immediate impression, attempting to sell drugs from his seat on center court.

The appearance marks Ali G's return ahead of an upcoming film featuring the character. Baron Cohen remained fully in character throughout the event, delivering the kind of provocative comedy the character is known for.

cards.headline: Universal Creates 8,800-Pound Trojan Horse for The Odyssey Premiere
cards.teaser: The studio constructed a massive replica for the London world premiere of Christopher Nolan's epic, which drew the director's largest ensemble cast.
cards.body:
Universal Pictures built an 8,800-pound Trojan horse for the world premiere of The Odyssey in London's Leicester Square. The premiere drew nearly the full cast of Christopher Nolan's epic film, making it the most star-studded event in the square this year.

Attendees included Nolan, Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, and Charlize Theron. The massive prop served as a centerpiece for the event, which celebrated the release of Nolan's adaptation of the classical Greek story.

cards.headline: Valérie Donzelli to Chair Venice Film Festival's Horizons Jury
cards.teaser: The French director will lead the international jury for the Horizons section at the 83rd Venice Film Festival.
cards.body:
The BBC News sources provided are about port sustainability and electric vehicle insurance—neither relates to the Venice Film Festival news.

I'm returning your original card text unchanged:

La Biennale di Venezia named the international juries for the Horizons section and the Luigi De Laurentiis Venice award for debut films at the upcoming 83rd Venice Film Festival. French director, actor, and screenwriter Valérie Donzelli will chair the Horizons jury.

Donzelli will be joined by American film distributor Peter Becker and Hong Kong-American director on the jury panel. The festival also announced the jury for the Luigi De Laurentiis award, which recognizes first-time filmmakers.

cards.headline: Panorama Studios Acquires Three Punjabi Films for Worldwide Release
cards.teaser: The Indian distributor secured theatrical rights to Argentina, Thaapi, and Ranjheya, all set for release in 2026.
cards.body:
Panorama Studios acquired worldwide theatrical distribution rights to three Punjabi-language films scheduled for 2026 release. The films are Argentina, starring Ammy Virk and Sargun Mehta; Thaapi, starring Neeru Bajwa and Sunny Singh; and Ranjheya, featuring Harrdy Sandhu, Simrat Kaur, and Angad Bedi.

The acquisition builds on the success of Ishqan De Lekhe, one of the studio's recent releases. Panorama Studios continues to expand its presence in regional Indian cinema with these three productions.

hero.headline: Senate Republicans and Trump at odds over surveillance, Iran policy, and filibuster
hero.teaser: Senate Majority Leader John Barrasso faces disagreements with the White House on multiple fronts as Congress returns from recess.
hero.body:
Senate Republicans Reject War Powers Resolution After Trump Pressure

President Trump faced off with Senate Republicans over military action in Iran, culminating in a dramatic reversal that underscores deepening tensions between the White House and GOP lawmakers.

The conflict began when Senate Republicans allowed a vote on a war powers resolution to block Trump's Iran operations. Angered by this defiance, Trump summoned GOP senators to a contentious lunch on Capitol Hill where he berated them over their opposition to his military strategy.

The confrontation grew particularly heated between Trump and Louisiana Senator Bill Cassidy, one of four Republicans who voted with Democrats on the measure. Trump questioned why anyone would support the War Powers Act. Cassidy responded directly, asking whether the question was rhetorical or genuine.

Despite the tense exchange, Cassidy's position shifted dramatically hours later. After receiving a personal briefing at the White House from Vice President JD Vance and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Cassidy returned to Capitol Hill and voted against a nearly identical war powers resolution that came up for a separate vote that evening.

"I want to thank Vice President Vance and Special Envoy Witkoff for the thorough briefing this afternoon on Iran," Cassidy posted on social media afterward. "I appreciate the quick invitation to the White House to address many of my concerns."

Republican Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky also shifted his stance, voting present on the second measure "to give the President more space and leverage to negotiate a lasting peace," according to his social media statement. Paul had previously voted with Democrats on the initial resolution.

The second war powers measure failed 47-50-1 just before midnight Wednesday, after which the Senate departed for a two-week recess. Senate Majority Leader John Thune and other GOP colleagues called Trump following the vote. Thune reported to reporters that Trump was "pleased with the outcome."

Trump subsequently thanked Thune in a social media post, noting that Cassidy and Paul had changed their positions. "This vote puts Iran on notice!" Trump wrote.

The two war powers votes occurred on separate tracks but addressed nearly identical concerns. Both measures were largely symbolic and do not carry the full force of law. The first passed the House and was then blocked by the Senate on Tuesday, followed by the second failed Senate vote on Wednesday.

The disputes over Iran policy form part of a broader disagreement between Trump and Senate Republicans. The two sides also remain at odds over extending surveillance authorities and Trump's push to eliminate the Senate filibuster to advance his legislative agenda, a proposal many Republican senators oppose as it would undermine their ability to block future Democratic initiatives.

cards.headline: Trump fires three members of Election Assistance Commission
cards.teaser: President Trump dismissed three members of the Election Assistance Commission last week, removing officials responsible for overseeing federal election security.
cards.body:
President Trump dismissed three members of the Election Assistance Commission last week, removing officials responsible for overseeing federal election security and voting system standards. Benjamin Hovland was among those fired from the bipartisan commission that helps states administer elections and certifies voting equipment.

The Election Assistance Commission was created after the 2000 presidential election to establish voting system guidelines and provide technical assistance to state and local election officials. The commission typically operates with four members, two from each party, who serve four-year terms and can only be removed for cause under federal law.

Hovland's dismissal comes as Congress prepares to return from recess to face what lawmakers describe as a lengthy agenda with limited time before the fall elections. The commission's work includes testing and certifying voting equipment used across the country, maintaining the National Voter Registration Form, and distributing federal funds to help states improve their election systems.

The timing of the firings has raised questions about election administration ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The commission has played a central role in helping states secure their voting systems and respond to cybersecurity threats since Russian interference in the 2016 election prompted increased federal attention to election security.

The White House has not provided detailed explanations for the dismissals. The three vacant seats leave the commission unable to conduct official business, as it requires a quorum to operate. Congress will need to confirm new appointees to restore the commission to full strength, a process that could take weeks or months depending on the confirmation schedule.

cards.headline: Congress returns with limited time and lengthy agenda
cards.teaser: Lawmakers face the loss of a senator, multiple policy debates, and a compressed legislative calendar.
cards.body:
Congress reconvenes this week with a lengthy to-do list and limited time before the fall elections. Lawmakers return to the sudden loss of a senator and pressure to address pending legislation on surveillance, defense policy, and appropriations.

The compressed calendar leaves little room for extended debates or procedural delays. House and Senate leaders will need to prioritize which measures to advance before the August recess and the final push before voters head to the polls in November.

cards.headline: House Republican leaders work to advance stalled legislative agenda
cards.teaser: GOP leaders face uncertain prospects for floor votes as lawmakers return to Washington.
cards.body:
Republican leaders in the House are working to resolve internal disagreements that have stalled the chamber's legislative agenda. Lawmakers return to uncertain prospects for bringing bills to the floor as time grows short before the election season intensifies.

The leadership scramble reflects ongoing divisions within the Republican conference over spending levels, policy riders, and procedural tactics. With a narrow majority, House Republicans need near-unanimous support to pass legislation without Democratic votes, making internal unity essential for advancing their priorities.

cards.headline: Democratic Party split deepens over progressive versus centrist direction
cards.teaser: Graham Platner's exit from the Maine Senate race has intensified internal party divisions.
cards.body:
The controversy surrounding Graham Platner's withdrawal from the Senate race in Maine has deepened a divide between progressive and centrist Democrats over the party's direction. Moderate Democrats say Platner's exit demonstrates their concern that the party has moved too far left in recent years.

The internal battle reflects broader tensions about Democratic messaging, policy priorities, and electoral strategy heading into the fall elections. Party leaders are working to manage the disagreements as they seek to maintain and expand their Senate majority.

cards.headline: Maine Democrats establish process to replace Platner as Senate candidate
cards.teaser: State party officials have created a system for selecting a new candidate after Graham Platner's departure.
cards.body:
Maine Democrats have established a process for choosing a replacement Senate candidate after Graham Platner withdrew from the race. Secretary of State Shenna Bellows has announced her candidacy for the nomination, joining other Democrats seeking to carry the party's banner in the competitive Senate contest.

Voters in Maine are adjusting to the sudden change in the race, which Democrats view as essential to their hopes of maintaining or expanding their Senate majority. The state party must move quickly to unite behind a new candidate and rebuild campaign operations with limited time before the general election.

cards.headline: Platner withdrawal may redirect Democratic donors to other Senate races
cards.teaser: Party fundraisers could shift focus to contests in Texas, Ohio, Iowa, North Carolina, and Alaska.
cards.body:
Graham Platner's exit from the Maine Senate race has created uncertainty among Democratic donors about where to invest their resources. With less than four months until the election, party fundraisers are reassessing their contribution strategy as Maine Democrats work to select and rally behind a replacement candidate.

Democrats remain focused on expanding their Senate majority, with competitive races in Texas, Ohio, Iowa, North Carolina, and Alaska also competing for donor attention. Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows is among those running to replace Platner in the Senate race.
